theory.overview: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is how AI learns to make decisions through trial and error. Unlike supervised learning with labeled data, RL agents interact with an environment, receiving rewards for good actions. This is how AlphaGo mastered Go, how robots learn to walk, and how game-playing AIs achieve superhuman performance. The core challenge is the credit assignment problem—determining which actions in a sequence led to eventual success or failure.

sections.title: The RL Framework
sections.content: RL models decision-making as interaction between an Agent and an Environment. The agent observes States, takes Actions, and receives Rewards.

components.name: Policy (π)
components.description: Agent's behavior: π(a|s) = probability of action a in state s

components.name: Episode
components.description: Sequence from start to terminal state

sections.title: The Goal: Maximize Return
sections.content: The agent aims to maximize cumulative discounted reward—balancing immediate and future gains.
sections.discountFactor: γ (gamma): 0 = greedy, 1 = far-sighted. Typically 0.99 for long-term tasks.
sections.intuition: $100 today is better than $100 in 10 years—discounting reflects uncertainty and time preference.

sections.title: Value Functions
sections.content: Value functions estimate how good it is to be in a state or take an action.

functions.name: State Value V(s)
functions.definition: Expected return starting from state s

functions.name: Action-Value Q(s,a)
functions.definition: Expected return taking action a in state s

sections.title: Q-Learning
sections.content: Model-free algorithm that learns optimal Q-values through experience. No need to know environment dynamics.
sections.explanation: Temporal Difference (TD) error: difference between current estimate and one-step lookahead target
components: α (alpha): learning rate—how aggressively we update
TD Target: r + γ max Q(s',a')—bootstrap from current Q-estimates
Bellman Optimality: Optimal Q satisfies Q*(s,a) = E[r + γ max Q*(s',a')]

sections.title: Exploration vs Exploitation
sections.content: Core dilemma: try new actions (explore) or stick with known good ones (exploit)?

strategies.name: ε-greedy
strategies.method: Random action with probability ε, else best

sections.title: Deep Q-Networks (DQN)
sections.content: Use neural networks to approximate Q-values for high-dimensional state spaces (e.g., Atari game pixels).

innovations.name: Experience Replay
innovations.purpose: Store and sample past experiences—breaks correlation, improves sample efficiency

innovations.name: Target Network
innovations.purpose: Separate network for computing TD targets—stabilizes learning

innovations.name: Frame Stacking
innovations.purpose: Stack 4 consecutive frames as state—captures motion

sections.architecture: CNN processing 84×84×4 input → FC layers → output Q-value for each action

sections.title: Policy Gradient Methods
sections.content: Directly optimize the policy by gradient ascent, rather than learning value function first.
sections.advantage: Works with continuous action spaces, can learn stochastic policies
sections.reinforce: $\nabla_\theta J(\theta) = \mathbb{E}[\nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a|s) \cdot G_t]$—increase probability of actions with high returns
sections.actorCritic: Combine policy gradient (actor) with value function (critic) for lower variance

keyConcepts.name: Markov Decision Process (MDP)
keyConcepts.description: Mathematical framework: states, actions, transition probabilities, rewards, discount factor.
keyConcepts.property: Markov property: future depends only on present state, not history

keyConcepts.name: Bellman Equation
keyConcepts.description: Recursive relationship between value of a state and its successors.

keyConcepts.name: Temporal Difference
keyConcepts.description: Learning method that bootstraps from current estimates—update based on observed reward plus discounted value of next state.
keyConcepts.contrast: Monte Carlo waits for episode end; TD learns after each step

keyConcepts.name: Experience Replay
keyConcepts.description: Store transitions in buffer, sample random batches for training.

complexity.dqn: $O(d^2)$ per step where d = network parameters—dominated by forward/backward pass
complexity.sampleEfficiency: RL is sample-inefficient—millions of interactions needed for complex tasks

steps.title: Environment Step
steps.description: Action affects environment, produces next state and reward.

steps.title: Q-Target
steps.description: Compute TD target using max future Q.

steps.title: TD Error
steps.description: Calculate difference between target and current estimate.

steps.title: Batch Training
steps.description: Sample batch and perform gradient descent.

practiceProblems.title: Q-Learning Update
practiceProblems.description: Current Q(s,a)=5. You take action, get reward r=2, next state has max Q(s')=8. α=0.1, γ=0.9. What's the new Q(s,a)?
practiceProblems.explanation: TD target incorporates immediate reward plus discounted future value. The update moves Q(s,a) 10% (α=0.1) toward this target.
hints: TD target = r + γ max Q(s')

practiceProblems.title: Exploration Decay
practiceProblems.description: Why does ε-greedy typically use decaying ε rather than fixed ε?
practiceProblems.answer: Early: need exploration to discover good actions. Late: should exploit known good policy. Decaying ε balances this transition.
practiceProblems.explanation: Initially Q-values are wrong (random initialization), so we explore. As Q converges to optimal values, exploration becomes wasteful. Common: ε from 1.0 decaying to 0.01 over training.

practiceProblems.title: Credit Assignment
practiceProblems.description: In a 100-move chess game, you only get reward at end (+1 win, -1 loss). How does the agent know which move was bad?
practiceProblems.answer: This is the credit assignment problem. Monte Carlo waits for episode end and attributes outcome to all moves. TD methods bootstrap, propagating value estimates backward.
practiceProblems.explanation: With only terminal rewards, Monte Carlo gives all moves in losing game equal blame. TD gradually propagates value estimates: states leading to bad outcomes get low V(s). Modern: Policy gradients with baselines reduce variance.

practiceProblems.title: Experience Replay Purpose
practiceProblems.description: Why does DQN use experience replay instead of just using each transition once and discarding?
practiceProblems.answer: (1) Break correlation: consecutive samples are similar, causing inefficient learning. (2) Sample efficiency: reuse rare transitions multiple times. (3) Smooths data distribution.
practiceProblems.explanation: Neural networks assume i.i.d. data. Consecutive game frames are highly correlated. Replay buffer allows random sampling, restoring independence. Rare but important transitions (e.g., falling off cliff) get reused.

practiceProblems.title: Deadly Triad
practiceProblems.description: What is the 'deadly triad' in RL and why is DQN vulnerable?
practiceProblems.answer: Function approximation + Bootstrapping + Off-policy learning = instability. DQN uses all three: neural network (FA), TD targets (bootstrapping), behavior≠target policy (off-policy).
practiceProblems.explanation: The deadly triad refers to why combining these three elements can cause divergence. Solutions: target networks (slowly updated), experience replay (breaks correlation), careful initialization. Modern methods like Rainbow DQN add more stabilizers.

practiceProblems.title: Policy vs Value Methods
practiceProblems.description: Compare policy gradient (REINFORCE) vs Q-learning. When would you prefer each?
practiceProblems.answer: Q-learning: discrete actions, deterministic, off-policy (efficient). Policy gradient: continuous actions, stochastic policies, better convergence properties. Continuous control (robotics) → policy methods. Discrete games → either.
practiceProblems.explanation: Q-learning needs max over actions—hard with continuous/infinite actions. Policy gradients work for any action space but have higher variance (need more samples). Actor-critic combines both: policy for actions, value for baseline.

minigame.title: GridWorld Navigator
minigame.description: Train an RL agent to navigate a grid world. Place rewards, traps, and goals. Watch Q-values propagate as the agent learns through trial and error. Compare Q-learning vs SARSA, explore vs exploit strategies.
instructions: Design grid: place start, goal, walls, traps, rewards
Set parameters: α (learning rate), γ (discount), ε (exploration)
Train agent: watch Q-values update in real-time
Visualize policy: arrows show best action per state
Test trained agent: see success rate

codeExample.code:
import numpy as np
import random
from collections import deque
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

class GridWorld:
    """
    Simple grid world environment
    """
    def __init__(self, size=5):
        self.size = size
        self.reset()
    
    def reset(self):
        self.agent_pos = (0, 0)
        self.goal = (self.size-1, self.size-1)
        return self._get_state()
    
    def _get_state(self):
        return self.agent_pos[0] * self.size + self.agent_pos[1]
    
    def step(self, action):
        # Actions: 0=up, 1=right, 2=down, 3=left
        moves = [(-1,0), (0,1), (1,0), (0,-1)]
        new_pos = (
            self.agent_pos[0] + moves[action][0],
            self.agent_pos[1] + moves[action][1]
        )
        
        # Check bounds
        if 0 <= new_pos[0] < self.size and 0 <= new_pos[1] < self.size:
            self.agent_pos = new_pos
        
        # Reward
        if self.agent_pos == self.goal:
            return self._get_state(), 10, True
        else:
            return self._get_state(), -1, False  # Small negative for each step

class QLearningAgent:
    """
    Tabular Q-learning agent
    """
    def __init__(self, n_states, n_actions, lr=0.1, gamma=0.9, epsilon=0.1):
        self.n_states = n_states
        self.n_actions = n_actions
        self.lr = lr
        self.gamma = gamma
        self.epsilon = epsilon
        self.Q = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))
    
    def select_action(self, state):
        if random.random() < self.epsilon:
            return random.randint(0, self.n_actions - 1)
        else:
            return np.argmax(self.Q[state])
    
    def update(self, state, action, reward, next_state, done):
        if done:
            target = reward
        else:
            target = reward + self.gamma * np.max(self.Q[next_state])
        
        td_error = target - self.Q[state, action]
        self.Q[state, action] += self.lr * td_error
        return td_error

class DQN(nn.Module):
    """
    Deep Q-Network for larger state spaces
    """
    def __init__(self, state_dim, action_dim, hidden_dim=64):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(state_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, action_dim)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x)

class DQNAgent:
    """
    DQN agent with experience replay
    """
    def __init__(self, state_dim, action_dim, lr=1e-3, gamma=0.99, epsilon=0.1):
        self.state_dim = state_dim
        self.action_dim = action_dim
        self.gamma = gamma
        self.epsilon = epsilon
        
        self.policy_net = DQN(state_dim, action_dim)
        self.target_net = DQN(state_dim, action_dim)
        self.target_net.load_state_dict(self.policy_net.state_dict())
        
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(self.policy_net.parameters(), lr=lr)
        self.memory = deque(maxlen=10000)
        self.batch_size = 64
    
    def select_action(self, state):
        if random.random() < self.epsilon:
            return random.randint(0, self.action_dim - 1)
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            state_tensor = torch.FloatTensor(state).unsqueeze(0)
            q_values = self.policy_net(state_tensor)
            return q_values.argmax().item()
    
    def store_transition(self, state, action, reward, next_state, done):
        self.memory.append((state, action, reward, next_state, done))
    
    def learn(self):
        if len(self.memory) < self.batch_size:
            return
        
        # Sample batch
        batch = random.sample(self.memory, self.batch_size)
        states, actions, rewards, next_states, dones = zip(*batch)
        
        states = torch.FloatTensor(states)
        actions = torch.LongTensor(actions)
        rewards = torch.FloatTensor(rewards)
        next_states = torch.FloatTensor(next_states)
        dones = torch.FloatTensor(dones)
        
        # Current Q values
        current_q = self.policy_net(states).gather(1, actions.unsqueeze(1))
        
        # Target Q values
        with torch.no_grad():
            next_q = self.target_net(next_states).max(1)[0]
            target_q = rewards + (1 - dones) * self.gamma * next_q
        
        # Loss and update
        loss = nn.MSELoss()(current_q.squeeze(), target_q)
        self.optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        self.optimizer.step()
        
        return loss.item()
    
    def update_target_network(self):
        self.target_net.load_state_dict(self.policy_net.state_dict())

def train_tabular_q_learning(env, agent, episodes=1000):
    """
    Train tabular Q-learning agent
    """
    episode_rewards = []
    
    for episode in range(episodes):
        state = env.reset()
        total_reward = 0
        done = False
        
        while not done:
            action = agent.select_action(state)
            next_state, reward, done = env.step(action)
            agent.update(state, action, reward, next_state, done)
            state = next_state
            total_reward += reward
        
        episode_rewards.append(total_reward)
        
        # Decay epsilon
        agent.epsilon = max(0.01, agent.epsilon * 0.995)
    
    return episode_rewards

def train_dqn(env, agent, episodes=1000, target_update=100):
    """
    Train DQN agent
    """
    episode_rewards = []
    
    for episode in range(episodes):
        state = env.reset()
        # One-hot encode state
        state_vec = np.zeros(env.size * env.size)
        state_vec[state] = 1
        
        total_reward = 0
        done = False
        
        while not done:
            action = agent.select_action(state_vec)
            next_state, reward, done = env.step(action)
            
            # One-hot encode next state
            next_state_vec = np.zeros(env.size * env.size)
            next_state_vec[next_state] = 1
            
            agent.store_transition(state_vec, action, reward, next_state_vec, done)
            agent.learn()
            
            state_vec = next_state_vec
            total_reward += reward
        
        episode_rewards.append(total_reward)
        
        # Update target network
        if episode % target_update == 0:
            agent.update_target_network()
        
        # Decay epsilon
        agent.epsilon = max(0.01, agent.epsilon * 0.995)
    
    return episode_rewards

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Create environment
    env = GridWorld(size=5)
    n_states = env.size * env.size
    n_actions = 4
    
    print("=== Q-Learning on 5×5 GridWorld ===\n")
    
    # Train Q-learning agent
    agent = QLearningAgent(n_states, n_actions, lr=0.1, gamma=0.9, epsilon=0.2)
    rewards = train_tabular_q_learning(env, agent, episodes=500)
    
    print(f"Average reward (last 100 episodes): {np.mean(rewards[-100:]):.2f}")
    print(f"Learned Q-values for start state:")
    print(f"  Up: {agent.Q[0, 0]:.2f}, Right: {agent.Q[0, 1]:.2f}, "
          f"Down: {agent.Q[0, 2]:.2f}, Left: {agent.Q[0, 3]:.2f}")
    
    # Show optimal policy
    print(f"\nOptimal policy (best action per state):")
    actions = ['↑', '→', '↓', '←']
    for i in range(env.size):
        row = []
        for j in range(env.size):
            state = i * env.size + j
            if (i, j) == env.goal:
                row.append('G')
            else:
                best_action = np.argmax(agent.Q[state])
                row.append(actions[best_action])
        print("  " + " ".join(row))
    
    print(f"\n=== DQN Example ===")
    dqn_agent = DQNAgent(n_states, n_actions)
    dqn_rewards = train_dqn(env, dqn_agent, episodes=500)
    print(f"DQN Average reward (last 100): {np.mean(dqn_rewards[-100:]):.2f}")
